title.value: Spot issues in routine contracts with legal AI tools

introduction.value: A commenter uses legal AI tools like Spellbook and CoCounsel to review standard-form contracts and spot issues before deciding whether a specialist is needed.

method.value: A commenter says they only DIY legal work that is procedural, repeatable, and easy to redo, including standard-form contract cleanup. Their workflow is to do the mechanical parts themselves, run the document through tools like Spellbook, AI Lawyer, or CoCounsel for a quick issue-spotting pass, and then decide whether the matter is routine enough to keep handling or needs a specialist.

outcome.value: The source gives no quantified results for the contract-review use case. The stated limit is that these tools help surface suspicious clauses, but they do not replace outside counsel's judgment about unusual risks or high-stakes matters.

notes.value: The main catch is scope: the commenter avoids DIY when consequences are irreversible, emotions distort judgment, or the facts are unusual.

Spot issues in routine contracts with legal AI tools
A commenter uses legal AI tools like Spellbook and CoCounsel to review standard-form contracts and spot issues before deciding whether a specialist is needed.
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
A commenter says they only DIY legal work that is procedural, repeatable, and easy to redo, including standard-form contract cleanup. Their workflow is to do the mechanical parts themselves, run the document through tools like Spellbook, AI Lawyer, or CoCounsel for a quick issue-spotting pass, and then decide whether the matter is routine enough to keep handling or needs a specialist.
How it went
The source gives no quantified results for the contract-review use case. The stated limit is that these tools help surface suspicious clauses, but they do not replace outside counsel's judgment about unusual risks or high-stakes matters.
Worth knowing
The main catch is scope: the commenter avoids DIY when consequences are irreversible, emotions distort judgment, or the facts are unusual.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I'm going to paste a standard-form [type of contract, e.g. NDA, vendor agreement, lease] and I'm on the [party, e.g. customer, tenant] side. Review it clause by clause and flag anything unusual, one-sided, missing, or risky, and rate each issue as low, medium, or high. Finish with a short list of the issues that would justify paying a specialist lawyer to look, and the questions I should ask them. Note that you are not a substitute for legal advice.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/Lawyertalk/comments/1qwy0es/are_there_any_legal_services_that_you_would_do
